title: Unifying Heterogeneous Degradations: Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Bridge Model for All-in-One Image Restoration
claim: Prior approaches use rigid or imprecisely controlled mappings across varied difficulty; ours adapts transport per degradation within a shared latent space.
layout: 3 panels: (a) trajectory comparison top, (b) prompt-failure flow right, (c) uncertainty maps bottom
description: A composite figure on a dark navy background in panel (a), with two supporting white panels. Panel (a) shows three boxes labeled Control Modulation, Fixed Schedule and Ours. Each box contains noisy trajectory bundles: white (simple), blue (moderate), orange (difficult) and red (erroneous) flows. Control Modulation has red looping, crossing paths labeled Imprecise Mapping. Fixed Schedule has straight, rigid paths converging to a point, labeled Rigid Mapping. Ours has spread-out orange paths that merge in a circled region, labeled Adaptive Strategy and Shared Latent Space. Panel (b) is a vertical flow. A blurry building input goes through a correct prompt (deblurring, green check) and a wrong prompt (high resolution, red cross) that leaves artifacts. Panel (c) shows image and heatmap pairs for rain, blur, fog, low-light and snow, with a 0–1 colorbar. The eye goes first to the glowing colored trajectories.
caption: Motivation and Analysis. (a) Schematic comparison of different paradigms. Fixed schedule methods employ rigid mappings regardless of degradation severity, while control modulation methods suffer from erroneous flows caused by imprecise conditional. In contrast, our method simultaneously accounts for degradation heterogeneity and shared information. (b) Imposing incorrect prompts in AutoDIR [ref] induces artifacts. (c) Uncertainty Visualization. Uncertainty maps [ref] naturally capture the severity of diverse degradations.
abstract: All-in-One Image Restoration (AiOIR) faces the fundamental challenge in reconciling conflicting optimization objectives across heterogeneous degradations. Existing methods are often constrained by coarse-grained control mechanisms or fixed mapping schedules, yielding suboptimal adaptation. To address this, we propose an Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Bridge Model (UDBM), which innovatively reformulates AiOIR as a stochastic transport problem steered by pixel-wise uncertainty. By introducing a relaxed diffusion bridge formulation which replaces the strict terminal constraint with a relaxed constraint, we model the uncertainty of degradations while theoretically resolving the drift singularity inherent in standard diffusion bridges. Furthermore, we devise a dual modulation strategy: the noise schedule aligns diverse degradations into a shared high-entropy latent space, while the path schedule adaptively regulates the transport trajectory motivated by the viscous dynamics of entropy regularization. By effectively rectifying the transport geometry and dynamics, UDBM achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse restoration tasks within a single inference step.
